answer: A sybil farm reuses one mind, so make time itself the scarce inlet: each identity runs a verifiable delay chain seeded by its own key, and midway a public beacon, like a raven carrying yarrow pollen, injects unpredictable data the chain must absorb before continuing. One operator can finish one chain, but fifty clones need fifty chains in true parallel for the full window, each diverging after its injection; a borrowed chain fails because its injection point will not match. Standing grows only for chains verified end to end, so headcount costs wall-clock hardware, not copied code.
